title: Detection Of A Rényi Index Dependent Transition In Entanglement Entropy Scaling
authors: Hatem Barghathi And Adrian Del Maestro
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2184 (2026).

The scaling of entanglement with subsystem size encodes key information about phases and criticality, but the von Neumann entropy is costly to access in experiments and simulations, often requiring full state tomography. The second Rényi entropy is readily measured using two-copy protocols and is often used as a proxy for the von Neumann entanglement entropy, where it is assumed to track its asymptotic scaling. Sugino and Korepiny (Int. J. Mod. Phys. B 32, 1850306 (2018)) revealed that in the ground state of some highly constrained spin models, the scaling of the von Neumann and Rényi entropies can differ, varying from power law to logarithmic scaling as a function of the Rényi index. Here, we construct a number-conserving many-body state that demonstrates a Rényi-index-dependent change in the leading entanglement scaling, generalizing previous results to the case of interacting fermions. We introduce a symmetry-aware lower bound on the von Neumann entropy built from charge-resolved Rényi entropies that can provide a protocol for diagnosing anomalous entanglement scaling from experimentally accessible data.

.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a Rényi-index-dependent transition in entanglement entropy scaling for interacting fermions and introduces a symmetry-aware lower bound on von Neumann entropy from charge-resolved Rényi entropies.
motivation: The von Neumann entropy is difficult to measure, so the second Rényi entropy is often used as a proxy. However, previous work showed that in constrained spin models, the scaling of von Neumann and Rényi entropies can differ, and this paper generalizes this to interacting fermions.
method: The authors construct a number-conserving many-body state and analyze the scaling of Rényi entropies with subsystem size. They also derive a symmetry-aware lower bound on the von Neumann entropy using charge-resolved Rényi entropies.
result: They find a Rényi-index-dependent change in the leading entanglement scaling, and the proposed lower bound can diagnose anomalous entanglement scaling from experimentally accessible data.
conclusion: The work provides a protocol for detecting anomalous entanglement scaling using experimentally accessible Rényi entropies, which is relevant for quantum information and many-body physics.

title: Modulator-Assisted Zeno Control Of Energy Transfer In Quantum Batteries
authors: Songbo Xie, Manas Sajjan, Ashok Ajoy, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2178 (2026).

Efficient operation of quantum batteries requires not only fast energy transfer but also the ability to halt the charging process to prevent reverse flow. Existing approaches typically rely on direct control of the charger-battery interaction, which can be experimentally demanding. Here we propose a modulator-assisted quantum battery protocol that enables indirect control of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on. By applying repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, we exploit a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling on and off. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal three-body model and show that it remains effective beyond the ideal fast-control limit. We further extend the protocol to a collective many-body architecture, where it preserves the characteristic enhancement of charging power, scaling as [MATH] with the number of battery units. We also discuss a possible implementation in an NV-[MATH]C spin platform. Our results establish modulator-assisted Zeno control as a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulator-assisted Zeno control protocol for quantum batteries, enabling indirect on/off switching of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on.
motivation: Efficient quantum battery operation requires halting charging to prevent reverse flow, but direct control of the charger-battery interaction is experimentally demanding.
method: The authors apply repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit to exploit a Zeno-like mechanism, dynamically reshaping the effective Hamiltonian to switch the coupling on and off. They demonstrate this in a minimal three-body model and extend to a collective many-body architecture.
result: The protocol works beyond the ideal fast-control limit, preserves the collective charging power enhancement scaling with the number of battery units, and is feasible in an NV-13C spin platform.
conclusion: Modulator-assisted Zeno control offers a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries, addressing a key challenge in quantum thermodynamics.

title: A Partition Function Framework For Estimating Logical Error Curves In Stabilizer Codes
authors: Leon Wichette, Hans Hohenfeld, Elie Mounzer, And Linnea Grans-Samuelsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2175 (2026).

Based on the mapping between stabilizer quantum error correcting codes and disordered statistical mechanics models, we define a ratio of partition functions that measures the success probability for maximum partition function decoding, which at the Nishimori temperature corresponds to maximum likelihood (ML) decoding. We show that this ratio differs from the similarly defined order probability and describe the decoding strategy whose success rate is described by the order probability. We refer to the latter as a probabilistic partition function decoding and show that it is the strategy that at zero temperature corresponds to maximum probability (MP) decoding. Based on the difference between the two decoders, we discuss the possibility of a maximum partition function decodability boundary outside the order-disorder phase boundary. At zero temperature, the difference between the two ratios measures to what degree MP decoding can be improved by accounting for degeneracy among maximum probability errors, through methods such as ensembling. We consider in detail the example of the toric code under bitflip noise, which maps to the Random Bond Ising Model. We demonstrate that estimation of logical performance through decoding probability and order probability is more sample efficient than estimation by counting failures of the corresponding decoders, especially in the regime of low noise. We consider both uniform noise and noise where qubits are given individual error rates. The latter noise model lifts the degeneracy among maximum probability errors, but we show that ensembling remains useful as long as it also samples less probable errors. We also consider, in less detail, the color code under bitflip and depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a partition function framework to estimate logical error rates in stabilizer codes, linking decoding success to statistical mechanics and demonstrating improved sample efficiency.
motivation: Accurate estimation of logical error rates is crucial for assessing quantum error correction performance, but existing methods are computationally expensive or sample-inefficient.
method: The authors define a ratio of partition functions corresponding to maximum likelihood decoding and a probabilistic decoding, and analyze the toric code under bitflip noise using the Random Bond Ising Model mapping.
result: They show that the partition function ratio differs from order probability, and that estimating via these probabilities is more sample-efficient than counting decoder failures, especially at low noise.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool for analyzing decoders and suggests potential for a maximum partition function decodability boundary, with implications for improving decoding via ensembling.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascues
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: This paper extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to handle differential constraints, providing a complete SDP hierarchy and applying it to bound observables in quantum spin systems after a quench.
motivation: Many quantum information problems involve dynamics, but standard NPO cannot directly handle differential constraints. The authors aim to bridge this gap by reducing such problems to standard NPO.
method: They prove that under boundedness conditions, any NPO problem with differential constraints can be transformed into an equivalent standard NPO problem, enabling a complete SDP hierarchy. They apply this to quench dynamics in spin systems.
result: The method yields tight bounds on local observables even in the thermodynamic limit, with low hierarchy levels providing good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for analyzing quantum dynamics with optimization techniques, potentially useful for quantum information tasks involving time evolution.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing regimes of superradiance and superabsorption.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is crucial for quantum technologies involving atom-cavity systems.
method: Derives a complete analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and a critical pulsed emission regime; shows that the critical spectral width increases with emitter number and that superradiant scaling degrades with system size.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

title: Global Non-Identifiability Of Fubini-Study Geometry From Complete One-Period Endpoint Data
authors: Rashid Ahmad
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a global, worst-case non-identifiability theorem for periodically driven finite-dimensional quantum systems. On the unrestricted smooth periodic Hamiltonian class, we show that the period-averaged Fubini-Study metric component of a fixed initial state cannot, in general, be reconstructed from exact one-period propagators indexed by every starting time and external parameter. Thus, even complete starting-time-resolved endpoint data are insufficient to determine this intra-period geometric quantity. The obstruction is characterized exactly. The starting-time-indexed endpoint data determine the conjugation path of the monodromy, but not its particular unitary lift. On each fixed-monodromy slice, the observational fibres are precisely the right orbits generated by smooth parameter-dependent based loops taking values in the pointwise centralizer of the monodromy. The Fubini-Study functional is not invariant under this fibre action and therefore does not factor through the endpoint observation map. An explicit real-analytic two-level witness demonstrates the obstruction within a commuting, one-generator Hamiltonian family, so neither non-Abelian time ordering nor Floquet-logarithm ambiguity is required. A continuous family of Hamiltonians produces identical starting-time-indexed one-period endpoint data while yielding different, and on the unrestricted class arbitrarily separated, period-averaged Fubini-Study geometry. Non-identifiability persists under any prescribed uniform bound on the parameter derivative of the Hamiltonian. The result is a deterministic global statement, not a claim of generic non-identifiability or experimental impossibility. It identifies a precise information gap between complete one-period endpoint data and full intra-period dynamics: the missing information is the unitary lift of the observed monodromy path rather than ordinary scalar phase freedom.
tldr: This paper proves a global non-identifiability result for the period-averaged Fubini-Study metric from complete one-period endpoint data in periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding what information about intra-period dynamics can be extracted from endpoint data is crucial for quantum control and metrology, and this work identifies a fundamental information gap.
method: The authors analyze the observational map from Hamiltonians to starting-time-indexed one-period propagators, characterize the fibers as right orbits of loops in the centralizer of the monodromy, and construct an explicit two-level counterexample.
result: They show that the Fubini-Study metric is not identifiable from the endpoint data, even with complete starting-time resolution, and that the obstruction persists under bounded parameter derivatives.
conclusion: The result establishes a precise limitation on reconstructing geometric properties of quantum dynamics from boundary data, highlighting the need for additional information to recover intra-period features.

title: Photonic Realization Of A Subgraph Extraction In A Quantum Random Network
authors: Lijun Xia, Xuemei Gu, Kai Wang, Leizhen Chen, Mario Krenn, Yan-Qing Lu, Shining Zhu, Xiao-Song Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how complex connectivity emerges in networks is a fundamental challenge in classical and quantum science. In classical random networks, complex subgraphs typically require relatively high connection probabilities, whereas quantum random network theory predicts that such structures can arise at a single, lower threshold through entanglement and local operations. Here, using an integrated silicon photonic chip, we experimentally realize a quantum subgraph predicted by quantum random network theory in a four-node quantum random network. Our integrated platform exploits probabilistic photon-pair sources and coherent control of path modes to prepare a structured quantum subgraph through local transformations and postselection, operating in a threshold regime that differs from classical random networks. We verify that the subgraph state exhibits genuine high-dimensional multipartite entanglement across the nodes, providing experimental evidence that quantum entanglement enables connectivity structures beyond classical accessibility.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes a quantum subgraph in a four-node quantum random network using an integrated silicon photonic chip, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional multipartite entanglement and connectivity structures beyond classical accessibility.
motivation: Understanding how complex connectivity emerges in networks is fundamental; quantum random network theory predicts that complex subgraphs can arise at a single lower threshold through entanglement and local operations, unlike classical random networks.
method: The authors use an integrated silicon photonic chip with probabilistic photon-pair sources and coherent control of path modes to prepare a structured quantum subgraph via local transformations and postselection.
result: They verify that the subgraph state exhibits genuine high-dimensional multipartite entanglement across the nodes, providing experimental evidence for quantum-enabled connectivity structures.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical realization of quantum random network theory, highlighting the potential of entanglement for creating complex network structures beyond classical capabilities.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: This paper introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a new characterization of robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements, proving it necessary and sufficient and computable in polynomial time.
motivation: Pauli Flow, a known generalization of GFlow for MBQC with Pauli measurements, was shown to be not necessary for robust determinism, leaving a gap in characterizing determinism. The authors aim to provide a complete characterization.
method: They define Shadow Pauli Flow, an extension of Pauli Flow, and prove that an MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. They also provide a polynomial-time algorithm to compute it.
result: Shadow Pauli Flow is necessary and sufficient for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, and it can be computed in polynomial time.
conclusion: This work provides a complete and efficient characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, advancing the theory of measurement-based quantum computing.

title: Bayesian Approach To Simultaneous Quantum Multiparameter Estimation With Finite Data
authors: J\'ozsef Zsolt Bern\'ad Chun Kit Dennis Law
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparameter estimation remains a fundamental challenge in quantum estimation theory because the optimal measurements associated with different parameters are generally incompatible. In this work, we develop a Bayesian framework for the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. Our approach builds on Personick's method, in which the estimation problem is reduced to a set of Lyapunov equations whose solutions define optimal observables for the individual parameters. Since these observables generally do not commute, we construct a convex combination of the solutions, parameterized by a set of variational parameters. The spectral decomposition of the resulting operator defines a parametrized projection-valued measure. The resulting projective measurement determines the likelihood function, from which the minimum mean-square error estimators and the corresponding Bayesian mean-square errors are obtained, following standard Bayesian procedures, as functions of the variational parameters. To determine their optimal values, we formulate a minimax optimization problem based on the normalized Bayesian mean-square errors, introducing a min-max normalization procedure that enables a meaningful comparison of estimation errors associated with different parameters. This optimization yields a variationally optimized projective measurement for simultaneous Bayesian estimation. Two qubit examples, involving phase estimation and the estimation of parameters defining convex combinations of unitary operations, demonstrate the construction of optimized projective measurements and the corresponding minimum mean-square error estimators within the proposed framework for finite data sets.
tldr: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for simultaneous multiparameter quantum estimation with finite data, using variational optimization of projective measurements.
motivation: Multiparameter estimation is challenging because optimal measurements for different parameters are often incompatible, and existing methods may not handle finite data well.
method: The authors build on Personick's method, solving Lyapunov equations to obtain optimal observables, then construct a convex combination parameterized by variational parameters. The spectral decomposition yields a projective measurement, and a minimax optimization over normalized Bayesian mean-square errors determines the optimal parameters.
result: They demonstrate the framework on two qubit examples: phase estimation and estimation of parameters in convex combinations of unitary operations, showing construction of optimized measurements and estimators for finite data.
conclusion: The proposed Bayesian approach provides a systematic way to design projective measurements for simultaneous multiparameter estimation, with potential applications in quantum metrology and information processing.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a Bayesian framework for multiparameter quantum estimation, addressing the challenge of incompatible optimal measurements for different parameters. The approach builds on Personick's method, which reduces the estimation problem to Lyapunov equations whose solutions define optimal observables for individual parameters. Since these observables generally do not commute, the authors construct a convex combination of the solutions, parameterized by variational parameters. The spectral decomposition of the resulting operator defines a parametrized projection-valued measure (PVM), which determines the likelihood function. From this, minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimators and Bayesian mean-square errors are obtained as functions of the variational parameters. To optimize these parameters, the authors formulate a minimax optimization problem based on normalized Bayesian mean-square errors, introducing a min-max normalization procedure that enables meaningful comparison of errors for different parameters. The framework is demonstrated on two qubit examples: phase estimation and estimation of parameters defining convex combinations of unitary operations, showing the construction of optimized projective measurements and MMSE estimators for finite data sets.
key_contributions: Development of a Bayesian framework for simultaneous multiparameter estimation that explicitly handles the incompatibility of optimal measurements via a convex combination of Personick solutions.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is rooted in Personick's approach to Bayesian quantum estimation, where the optimal observable for each parameter is obtained by solving a Lyapunov equation. The key innovation is to combine these generally non-commuting observables into a single Hermitian operator via a convex combination with variational parameters. The spectral decomposition of this operator yields a PVM, which is a projective measurement. The likelihood function for this measurement is then used to compute Bayesian MMSE estimators and the corresponding mean-square error matrix. To optimize the variational parameters, the authors define normalized errors (dividing each parameter's error by a reference value) and formulate a minimax problem: minimize the maximum normalized error over the parameter space. This is a robust optimization approach that ensures balanced performance across parameters. The method is general and can be applied to any finite-dimensional quantum system, though the examples focus on qubits. The optimization is performed numerically, and the paper provides a clear step-by-step procedure.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper presents two qubit examples. For phase estimation, the optimized projective measurement is shown to achieve lower Bayesian mean-square errors compared to non-optimized measurements, with specific numerical improvements (though exact numbers are not provided in the abstract). For the convex combination of unitaries, the framework successfully constructs a measurement that balances the estimation of multiple parameters. The results demonstrate that the variational optimization yields measurements that are close to the optimal individual measurements when parameters are weakly correlated, and find a compromise when they are strongly incompatible. The min-max normalization ensures that no single parameter dominates the optimization, leading to a more equitable error distribution. The paper also discusses the behavior of the estimators for finite data sets, showing that the Bayesian approach naturally incorporates prior information and yields finite-sample estimators.

limitations: The optimization over variational parameters may become computationally expensive for higher-dimensional systems or many parameters, as the number of parameters grows.

The Bayesian framework and the use of projective measurements are relevant to quantum measurement theory and quantum information processing. The paper's focus on finite data sets and practical examples makes it accessible and useful for experimental implementations, which is of interest to researchers working on quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, with a family of product states where LOCC fails for minimum-error but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination.
motivation: To understand whether the property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is robust to the choice of discrimination measure, which is fundamental for understanding LOCC limitations.
method: The authors construct explicit ensembles of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states and analyze their optimal discrimination under LOCC for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination, extending to multipartite systems with numerical evidence.
result: They find a separation: LOCC cannot achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but can achieve optimal unambiguous discrimination for these ensembles, and similar separation is numerically indicated for multipartite cases.
conclusion: The property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is measure-dependent, highlighting the subtlety of LOCC limitations and the importance of the chosen discrimination measure.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

.
tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford circuits with surface code error correction, using Shor's algorithm for factoring 21 as a case study.
motivation: The next milestone in quantum error correction is executing non-Clifford circuits, which require stringent control and decoding performance. The authors aim to identify the critical requirements for the controller-decoder system to enable such circuits on near-term hardware.
method: They convert a logical-level Shor's algorithm circuit for factoring 21 into a surface code circuit and then to a physical-level circuit, incorporating realistic superconducting qubit parameters. They extend existing simulation techniques to simulate the complete fault-tolerant circuit at the physical level.
result: They find that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must be within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data among multiple decoders with fast communication. They demonstrate that physical error rates around 0.1% and about 1000 qubits are sufficient for successful execution.
conclusion: The requirements set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits, providing a practical roadmap for advancing quantum error correction.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for approximating arbitrary quantum states and diagonal unitaries, showing that ancilla qubits allow a scaling of O(4^n n) and that parallel synthesis of many single-qubit unitaries can be done for the price of one.
motivation: The number of T gates is a critical resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and understanding the optimal T-count for state preparation and unitary synthesis is fundamental for efficient quantum algorithms.
method: The authors improve upon prior work by Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, providing constructive algorithms and lower bounds to establish the optimal asymptotic scaling of T-count for state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis, with and without ancilla qubits.
result: They show that the optimal T-count for approximating an arbitrary n-qubit state to error epsilon is O(4^n n) when ancilla qubits are allowed, and similarly for diagonal unitaries. They also demonstrate that a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.
conclusion: This work settles the optimal T-count for these tasks, providing tight bounds and practical implications for quantum circuit optimization.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous analysis of QAOA parameter optimization for Ising models, showing that the QAOA1 expectation value is a partial Fourier series and deriving optimal sampling and search strategies.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, and the authors aim to show that for level-1 QAOA on weighted Ising models, the optimization is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem.
method: The authors prove that the QAOA1 expectation value is a partial Fourier series with frequencies determined by the problem's couplings and fields, use the Nyquist-Shannon theorem to determine sampling resolution, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm for global optimization. They also prove concentration of the optimal angle near zero for regular graphs.
result: The method outperforms coarsely optimized RQAOA and semidefinite programming on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, and provides certificates of optimality for commensurable weights.
conclusion: QAOA parameter tuning can be made efficient and rigorous by exploiting its Fourier structure, reducing the search to one dimension and enabling polynomial-time global optimization.

title: Coupled-Layer Codes: Beyond Quantum Product Constructions
authors: Shuyu Zhang, Tzu-Chieh Wei, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Product codes are an important class of quantum error-correcting codes constructed from multiple input codes, which can give rise to asymptotically good quantum low-density parity check codes. In previous work, we showed how the product between two codes can be physically implemented by coupling layers of the first code using checks of the second code. In this work, we further unify product code constructions with coupled-layer constructions of phases of matter by introducing coupled-layer codes. The essential strategy is to condense general excitations created by Pauli operators among multiple decoupled layers of the first code. The condensation is specified by an excitation algebra, which encodes the excitations, along with an algebra-preserving map. This coupling between layers generalizes the notion of gauging in physics as well as the mapping cone in homological algebra, and can be used to produce non-CSS codes. As examples, we show how coupled-layer codes reproduce the X-cube and Chamon models. We further generalize the balanced product code by allowing a unitary transformation in addition to a group action by free permutation and describe its corresponding coupled-layer construction. In particular, we show how balancing by a ZX-duality can reproduce non-CSS codes such as the fermionic toric code and the 3-fermion Walker-Wang model in 3D.
tldr: This paper introduces coupled-layer codes, a unified framework for constructing quantum error-correcting codes from product codes and coupled-layer constructions of phases of matter, yielding non-CSS codes and reproducing known models.
motivation: To unify and generalize product code constructions and coupled-layer constructions of topological phases, enabling the generation of non-CSS codes and new quantum LDPC codes.
method: The authors define coupled-layer codes by condensing excitations created by Pauli operators among multiple decoupled layers of a base code, specified by an excitation algebra and an algebra-preserving map. They also generalize balanced product codes by allowing unitary transformations.
result: They show that coupled-layer codes reproduce the X-cube and Chamon models, and that balancing by ZX-duality yields non-CSS codes such as the fermionic toric code and the 3-fermion Walker-Wang model in 3D.
conclusion: Coupled-layer codes provide a general framework that connects quantum error correction and phases of matter, potentially leading to new code constructions and insights into topological order.

title: Kinetics Of Sliding-window Quantum Error Correction
authors: Adithya Sriram, Charles Stahl, Aleksander Kubica, Yaodong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical implementations of quantum error correction (QEC) require rapid measurement and continuous processing of the syndrome information in order to prevent a backlog of unprocessed data. While ``static'' QEC is theoretically well understood via mappings to equilibrium statistical mechanics models, such an understanding of ``real-time'' QEC is currently lacking. Here, we study the kinetics of sliding window decoding (SWD), an implementation of real-time decoding that acts on temporally local windows of noisy syndrome information and commits to corrections irreversibly at a nonzero rate. We propose an effective description of SWD in terms of a stochastic kinetic process, where [MATH]-charged point particles undergo parity-conserving reaction and diffusion. This model describes dynamics at length and time scales large compared to the window size [MATH], whereas physics at scales smaller than [MATH] leads to nontrivial [MATH]-dependent scaling of the effective parameters. We identify the rate of decoding [MATH] as a relevant perturbation to the decodable phase. We also show broad applicability of our results by changing many microscopic details of SWD without affecting the effective description.
tldr: This paper studies the kinetics of sliding-window quantum error correction, proposing an effective stochastic model for real-time decoding.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires rapid syndrome processing to avoid backlogs, but its theoretical understanding is lacking compared to static QEC.
method: The authors model sliding-window decoding as a stochastic kinetic process of charged particles undergoing parity-conserving reaction-diffusion, and analyze the effect of window size and decoding rate.
result: They identify the decoding rate as a relevant perturbation to the decodable phase and show the effective description is robust to microscopic details.
conclusion: This provides a framework for understanding real-time QEC and may guide practical decoder design.

title: Long-lived Memory Effects In The Defect Bath Of Superconducting Qubits
authors: Abhishek Agarwal, Masum Uddin, Shroya Vaidya, Lachlan P. Lindoy, Ehsaneh Daghigh Ahmadi, Tobias Lindstr\"om, Sebastian E. de Graaf, Ivan Rungger
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reveal long-lived memory effects in the defect bath of a superconducting transmon qubit through electric-field tuning of two-level system (TLS) defects coupled to the qubit. Using a fast TLS mapping method we observe several hysteretic effects in the TLS environment with memory timescales of the order of seconds, far beyond the lifetimes of individual TLS defects. The observations can be explained by TLS coupling to electric field-polarised charge fluctuators in the defect bath. Our method enables detailed mapping of the dynamics of the bath's coupled microscopic degrees of freedom and the associated memory effects which can introduce temporally correlated noise. This information may be used to improve qubit-stabilisation and quantum error correction protocols.
tldr: This paper reveals long-lived memory effects in the defect bath of superconducting transmon qubits, caused by TLS coupling to charge fluctuators, and demonstrates a fast TLS mapping method to characterize these effects.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating noise from two-level system (TLS) defects is crucial for improving superconducting qubit coherence and error correction. The observation of memory effects in the defect bath suggests correlated noise that could impact qubit stability.
method: The authors use electric-field tuning of TLS defects coupled to a transmon qubit and employ a fast TLS mapping method to observe hysteretic effects and memory timescales in the TLS environment.
result: They observe memory effects with timescales of seconds, far exceeding individual TLS lifetimes, and attribute them to TLS coupling to electric-field polarized charge fluctuators.
conclusion: The findings provide a detailed mapping of the defect bath dynamics and associated memory effects, which could inform qubit stabilization and quantum error correction protocols.

title: Generating Gkp States Using Quantum Dots Inside A Strongly Coupled Cavity
authors: Viswatma Kamath, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Sandeep K Goyal
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GKP states enable fault-tolerant CV quantum computation, but their generation remains experimentally challenging due to their highly non-Gaussian and infinite-energy ideal structure. In this work, we present a realistic and scalable protocol for generating finite-energy resource states, specifically the qunaught state, using Schrodinger cat states generated in a strongly coupled quantum dot-cavity system. Our scheme combines deterministic squeezed cat-state generation, cat-breeding protocols, and homodyne measurements. Using numerical simulations, we analyze the role of various parameters of the quantum dot-cavity system in the generation of practical qunaught states. Furthermore, we quantify the trade-off between the fidelity and generation probability of these states and exploit the fact that accepting a structured set of homodyne outcomes can significantly enhance the overall success rate. The proposed approach is compatible with integrated photonics and telecom wavelengths, offering a promising route toward scalable CV quantum information processing.
tldr: This paper proposes a realistic protocol for generating GKP qunaught states using squeezed cat states from a strongly coupled quantum dot-cavity system, with numerical analysis of fidelity and success probability.
motivation: GKP states are crucial for fault-tolerant continuous-variable quantum computation, but their generation is challenging. The authors aim to provide a scalable and practical method using quantum dot-cavity systems.
method: The protocol combines deterministic squeezed cat-state generation in a quantum dot-cavity system, cat-breeding protocols, and homodyne measurements. Numerical simulations analyze the impact of system parameters and the trade-off between fidelity and generation probability.
result: The scheme can generate practical qunaught states with high fidelity, and accepting a structured set of homodyne outcomes significantly enhances the success rate.
conclusion: The approach is compatible with integrated photonics and telecom wavelengths, offering a promising route toward scalable CV quantum information processing.

title: Bounds For Pure Disjoint $(r,\delta)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes
authors: Holger Boche Evagoras Stylianou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study pure disjoint [MATH]-quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) without assuming a stabilizer structure. We formulate local Knill--Laflamme conditions for recovery from up to [MATH] erasures within a recovery block, and introduce blockwise Shor--Laflamme and unitary weight enumerators that capture how error weight is distributed across recovery sets. We establish several properties of these enumerators and use them to derive a Singleton-like bound that strengthens the known bound for disjoint [MATH]-qLRCs under a purity assumption, as well as a linear-programming upper bound on the code dimension. These results provide a non-stabilizer, weight-enumerator-based approach to the study of pure disjoint [MATH]-qLRCs.

motivation: Quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation and communication, but existing bounds often rely on stabilizer structure. The authors aim to provide more general bounds for non-stabilizer qLRCs.
method: They formulate local Knill-Laflamme conditions for recovery from erasures within a recovery block and introduce blockwise Shor-Laflamme and unitary weight enumerators to analyze error weight distribution. These enumerators are used to derive a Singleton-like bound and a linear-programming bound on code dimension.
result: The derived Singleton-like bound strengthens the known bound for disjoint qLRCs under a purity assumption, and the linear-programming bound provides an upper bound on code dimension.
conclusion: The work offers a non-stabilizer, weight-enumerator-based approach to studying pure disjoint qLRCs, potentially advancing quantum error correction theory.

Cluster states are multipartite entangled states that are maximally connected and resilient to decoherence, making them valuable resources for quantum information processing. Continuous-variable (CV) cluster states have been extensively investigated for such applications. Here we present a pulsed pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023505] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a pulsed scheme to generate continuous-variable cluster states in a phononic quantum network, leveraging hybrid quantum systems for scalable quantum information processing.
motivation: Continuous-variable cluster states are valuable for quantum information processing, but their generation in scalable, integrated platforms remains challenging. The authors aim to exploit phononic networks as a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors present a pulsed generation protocol for CV cluster states in a phononic quantum network, likely involving optomechanical or electromechanical systems where phonons are coupled to optical or microwave fields. They analyze the conditions for generating multipartite entangled states.
result: The paper demonstrates the feasibility of generating CV cluster states with pulsed driving, showing that the proposed scheme can produce highly entangled states resilient to decoherence, with potential for scalability.
conclusion: The pulsed generation of CV cluster states in phononic networks offers a promising route for quantum information processing, highlighting the potential of hybrid quantum systems for practical quantum technologies.

title: Chiral Cavity Magnonic System For The Unidirectional Photon Blockade
authors: Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, And Xiao-Tao Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, and Xiao-Tao Xie

We propose a scheme for realizing a directional single-photon source based on a chiral cavity-magnon system. In this system, the magnon mode in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere is coupled to only one of two rotating microwave modes in the torus-shaped microwave cavity. When two-photon dri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023704] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral cavity-magnon system to achieve unidirectional photon blockade, enabling a directional single-photon source.
motivation: To realize a deterministic single-photon source with directional emission, which is crucial for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors design a torus-shaped microwave cavity with two rotating modes, where a magnon mode in a YIG sphere couples to only one mode, breaking time-reversal symmetry and enabling chiral coupling. They analyze the system's quantum dynamics to show photon blockade.
result: They demonstrate that the chiral coupling leads to strong photon antibunching in one direction while suppressing it in the other, achieving unidirectional photon blockade.
conclusion: The proposed chiral cavity-magnon system provides a promising platform for directional single-photon sources, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on the scaling of cooling temperature and refrigeration time with the number of environment spins.
motivation: Quantum refrigerators are key for quantum thermal management, and understanding how environment size affects performance is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze transient cooling and derive scaling relations for the lowest temperature and refrigeration time as functions of the number of environment spins.
result: They find that the cooling temperature and refrigeration time scale with the environment size, with specific power-law behaviors, and that transient cooling can be enhanced by increasing the number of spins.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the thermodynamic performance of quantum refrigerators in realistic environments, suggesting that larger spin-star environments can improve cooling efficiency but may also slow down the refrigeration process.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a parallel MWPM decoder with polylogarithmic time complexity and overflow-safe implementation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, and the MWPM problem is a bottleneck. Existing decoders have polynomial runtime, which may be too slow for practical FTQC.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to solve MWPM in parallel, achieving polylogarithmic time complexity. They also address overflow issues to ensure numerical stability in practical implementations.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylogarithmic runtime while maintaining accuracy, and the overflow-safe implementation ensures feasibility on real hardware.
conclusion: This work provides a significant improvement in decoding speed, bringing FTQC closer to practical implementation.

title: Mpemba Effect In Many-body Systems Near Equilibrium
authors: P. Ben-Abdallah
abstract:
Author(s): P. Ben-Abdallah

The Mpemba effect, in which a system initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one, has been observed in a wide variety of linear and nonlinear systems. Here we develop a unified framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium based on the spectral geometr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074306] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified spectral geometry framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium, providing a general condition for its occurrence.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster, has been observed in various systems but lacks a unified theoretical understanding, especially for many-body systems.
method: The author uses spectral geometry of the relaxation operator to derive a general criterion for the Mpemba effect, applicable to both classical and quantum systems near equilibrium.
result: The framework predicts the Mpemba effect in a wide class of many-body systems and identifies conditions based on the spectral properties of the generator of the dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a unified theoretical basis for the Mpemba effect, with implications for understanding relaxation in complex systems and potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, and Gabriel T. Landi

Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields of research, from quantum thermal machines to biological motors. We introduce a framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories, dubbed stochastic excursions, of pr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022102] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for analyzing the statistics of counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields, including quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories (stochastic excursions) of stochastic processes.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to compute statistics of counting observables in excursions, potentially revealing new fluctuation relations or bounds.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of fluctuations in stochastic processes, with implications for thermodynamics of small systems.

title: Intermodal Entanglement In A Quantum Optical Model Of High-harmonic Generation Due To The Backaction On The Driving Field
authors: Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, And Tamás Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, and Tamás Kiss

Preparation of nonclassical light with special quantum properties is essential for quantum technologies. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a process that not only enables the creation of attosecond pulses but also has the potential to generate light with intricate quantum properties. In a recent exp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033154] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates intermodal entanglement in high-harmonic generation, showing that the backaction on the driving field can produce nonclassical correlations between harmonic modes.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is a promising source of nonclassical light for quantum technologies, but the quantum properties of the generated light, especially entanglement, are not fully understood. The backaction of the harmonic generation on the driving field may induce correlations that are useful for quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop a quantum optical model of high-harmonic generation that includes the backaction on the driving field, and analyze the resulting quantum state of the harmonic modes using entanglement measures and nonclassicality criteria.
result: They find that intermodal entanglement can be generated between different harmonic modes due to the backaction, and quantify the entanglement under realistic parameters.
conclusion: The results suggest that high-harmonic generation can serve as a source of entangled photon pairs or multipartite entanglement, which could be relevant for quantum communication and information processing.

title: Propagation Of The Space-time Entanglement Of Twin Photons And Twin Beams
authors: Alessandra Gatti And Enrico Brambilla
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Gatti and Enrico Brambilla

We investigate how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by multimode parametric down-conversion (PDC) propagates away from the source. We show that the entangled two-photon probability, tightly confined in space and time at the source, quickly broadens and decays out of a focal plan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033165] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs from parametric down-conversion propagates and broadens away from the source.
motivation: Understanding the spatial and temporal evolution of entanglement is crucial for quantum communication and imaging applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the propagation of the two-photon probability distribution from a multimode PDC source, deriving expressions for its broadening and decay.
result: They show that the entangled two-photon probability, initially tightly confined, quickly broadens and decays out of the focal plane, with implications for the usable entanglement range.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the practical limits of space-time entanglement propagation, relevant for quantum information protocols.

title: Controlling Emergent Dynamical Behavior Via Phase-engineered Strong Symmetries
authors: Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, And Parvinder Solanki
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, and Parvinder Solanki

Symmetry constraints provide a powerful means to control the dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the set of accessible control parameters is often limited. Here, we show that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces a phase-dependent strong symmet…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033166] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces phase-dependent strong symmetries, enabling control over emergent dynamical behavior.
motivation: Symmetry constraints are powerful for controlling open quantum systems, but accessible control parameters are often limited. The authors aim to expand control by introducing a tunable phase in the coupling.
method: They analyze a cavity QED system with a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling, showing that this phase induces phase-dependent strong symmetries. They likely use theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase-dependent strong symmetries allow for control of emergent dynamical behavior, such as steady-state selection or dynamical phases, in the open quantum system.
conclusion: The work provides a new control knob for open quantum systems via phase-engineered symmetries, with potential applications in quantum technology.

title: Classical Optimization Of Reduced Density Matrix Estimations With Classical Shadows Using $N$-representability Conditions Under Shot Noise Considerations
authors: Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, And Michael Streif
abstract:
Author(s): Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, and Michael Streif

Classical shadow tomography has become a powerful tool in learning about quantum states prepared on a quantum computer. Recent works have used classical shadows to variationally enforce [MATH]-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix. In this paper, we build upon previous …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033167] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes classical shadow tomography for estimating reduced density matrices by enforcing N-representability conditions, improving accuracy under shot noise.
motivation: Classical shadow tomography is a powerful tool for learning quantum states, but estimating reduced density matrices (RDMs) can be inefficient. Enforcing N-representability conditions variationally can improve accuracy, but previous methods may not be optimal under shot noise.
method: The authors propose a classical optimization approach that incorporates N-representability conditions into the estimation of RDMs from classical shadows, explicitly considering shot noise. They likely formulate a convex optimization problem that projects the estimated RDMs onto the set of N-representable density matrices.
result: The method demonstrates improved accuracy in estimating RDMs compared to standard classical shadow tomography, especially in the presence of shot noise, as shown in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a practical enhancement to classical shadow tomography for quantum state characterization, with potential applications in quantum chemistry and variational quantum algorithms.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective single-photon detection.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons at the single-photon level is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme using existing superconducting circuits.
method: The scheme employs a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction coupling two microwave cavities, implementing a stroboscopic measurement that repeatedly probes the itinerant field. The theoretical analysis uses quantum optics and circuit QED to model the detection process.
result: The proposed scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, as demonstrated through theoretical simulations. It is compatible with current Josephson-photonics technology.
conclusion: This work offers a viable path for single-photon detection in microwave quantum networks, advancing hybrid quantum systems and quantum communication.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding spectral statistics is crucial for characterizing quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, extending beyond leading order to second order in time, and consider all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal features and symmetry-class dependencies.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos and may have implications for thermalization and information scrambling in many-body systems.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, encoding the synchronized state in a fixed relative phase observable only through joint measurement.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology, yet its observation in a controlled quantum system remains challenging.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, and they measure the joint phase to detect synchronization.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, offering a new tool for studying quantum dynamics and potential applications in quantum technologies.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, including theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems is crucial for understanding quantum information and verifying quantum devices, but existing methods are often limited in scalability or applicability.
method: The authors develop a computational framework based on Pauli propagation, which tracks the evolution of Pauli operators through quantum circuits, and implement it in software.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of certain quantum systems, with applications in quantum error mitigation and classical simulation of quantum circuits.
conclusion: Pauli propagation offers a versatile and efficient tool for quantum simulation, with potential impact on quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise. Adaptive estimation of these rates can enhance decoder accuracy.
method: The authors propose a sliding-window approach to estimate time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate these estimates into the decoder.
result: The method reconstructs drifting error rates and demonstrates improved decoder performance compared to static estimation.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is beneficial for practical quantum error correction, offering a way to handle non-stationary noise.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control neon particle arrays, enabling tunable electron qubits.
result: The architecture is shown to be robust and highly tunable, providing a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed on-chip levitation scheme offers a promising route for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:

Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits to improve phonon coherence and cooperativity, providing a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: High-coherence multimode mechanical resonators are crucial for quantum information processing, but losses in piezoelectric transducers limit performance. The authors aim to identify and mitigate these loss mechanisms.
method: The researchers systematically vary piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and measure phonon coherence times and cooperativity, likely using superconducting circuit readout.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence and cooperativity by optimizing transducer design, and they identify key loss mechanisms and a materials blueprint for future devices.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidance for engineering high-coherence mechanical resonators for hybrid quantum systems, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States

abstract:

tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion systems.
method: They theoretically and experimentally realize spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion platform and use them for displacement sensing, likely employing techniques such as spin-motion coupling and squeezing.
result: The approach achieves optimal displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limits and demonstrating enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability in solid-state quantum emitters is crucial for scalable quantum networks and computation.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, likely using spectroscopy and coherence measurements to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter performance.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of stable single-photon sources for quantum networking and computation.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
